test_title: PYST 62: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a correct match of tissue type and its example?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Connective tissue – Blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Connective tissue** is the most diverse and abundant type of tissue in the **human body**, providing support, protection, and structural integration. **Blood** is classified as a **fluid connective tissue** because it consists of cells (**erythrocytes, leukocytes, and platelets**) suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix called **plasma**, and it serves to connect all systems of the body by transporting nutrients and waste. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Epithelial tissue** consists of tightly packed cells that form a continuous sheet, covering the external surfaces of the body and lining internal organs and cavities. **Blood** does not belong to this category; rather, epithelial tissue examples include the **epidermis of the skin** and the **inner lining of the mouth**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Muscular tissue** is specialized for **contraction** and movement. It is composed of long cells called **muscle fibers**. **Neurons**, however, are the functional units of the **nervous system**, not the muscular system. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Nervous tissue** is responsible for receiving stimuli and transmitting electrical impulses to various parts of the body. It consists of **neurons** and **glial cells**. **Muscles** are effector organs composed of **muscular tissue** that respond to nervous stimulation, but they are not nervous tissue themselves. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Animal tissues are categorized into four primary types based on their structure and function: **Epithelial**, **Connective**, **Muscular**, and **Nervous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Connective Tissue:**
 
 
• **Loose Connective Tissue:** Includes **Areolar tissue** (found under the skin) and **Adipose tissue** (stores **fat**).
 
• **Dense Connective Tissue:** Includes **Tendons** (connect **muscle to bone**) and **Ligaments** (connect **bone to bone**).
 
• **Specialized Connective Tissue:** Includes **Cartilage**, **Bone**, and **Blood**. Unlike other connective tissues, **blood** does not contain **fibers** like **collagen** or **elastin** unless it is clotting.
 
 
 
• **Components of Blood:**
 
 
• **Plasma:** A straw-colored fluid making up about **55%** of total blood volume, containing water, proteins, and electrolytes.
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs):** Also known as **Erythrocytes**, containing **hemoglobin** for **oxygen transport**.
 
• **White Blood Cells (WBCs):** Also known as **Leukocytes**, which are part of the **immune system**.
 
• **Platelets:** Also known as **Thrombocytes**, which aid in **blood clotting**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Tissues:**
 
 
• **Epithelial:** Functions include **protection**, **secretion**, **absorption**, and **filtration**.
 
• **Muscular:** Categorized into **Skeletal** (voluntary), **Smooth** (involuntary, found in **visceral organs**), and **Cardiac** (found in the **heart**).
 
• **Nervous:** Specialized for **excitability** and **conductivity**, allowing the body to respond to internal and external environmental changes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin:** Most connective tissues, including **blood** and **bone**, originate from the **mesoderm** (the middle germ layer of the embryo).
 
• **Physical Properties of Blood:** The average adult human has about **5 to 6 liters** of blood. The **pH** of human blood is slightly **alkaline**, typically ranging from **7.35 to 7.45**.
 
• **Nervous System Unit:** The **Neuron** is the longest cell in the human body, specifically designed to transmit signals over long distances, such as from the **spinal cord** to the **toes**.
 
• **Bone vs. Cartilage:** While both are specialized connective tissues, **bone** has a hard, **calcified matrix**, whereas **cartilage** has a firm but **flexible matrix** composed of **chondroitin salts**.
